root_cause.text: In `net/bluetooth/mgmt.c`’s `tlv_data_is_valid()`, the Bluetooth MGMT advertising TLV parser accessed `data[i + 1]` to check the element type before first verifying that the current length-delimited field actually contained that byte, allowing an out-of-bounds read when a malformed `MGMT_OP_ADD_ADVERTISING` request placed the length byte at the end of the buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `tlv_data_is_valid()` “reads each advertising data field length from `data[i]`, then inspects `data[i + 1]` … before checking that the current field still fits inside the supplied buffer,” and the patch moves `if (i + cur_len >= len) return false;` ahead of the `data[i + 1] == ...` type checks to ensure the type byte is in-bounds first.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject invalid TLV records whose length exceeds the remaining buffer to prevent unsafe parsing.
intent_record.what: In tlv_data_is_valid(), a new bounds check was added after reading the current field length: if the field would extend past the total buffer length (`i + cur_len >= len`), the function now returns false. A comment explaining this invalid-length condition was also inserted.
intent_record.how: At runtime, malformed TLV/EIR data whose declared length would run beyond the end of the provided buffer is now rejected immediately instead of being further processed. This prevents out-of-bounds parsing of advertising data and treats truncated or inconsistent records as invalid.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the TLV field length overrun validation from `tlv_data_is_valid()`.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a bounds-checking block from `tlv_data_is_valid()`: the comment explaining that a current field length exceeding the total data length is invalid, and the conditional `if (i + cur_len >= len) return false;` were deleted from the loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer rejects TLV/EIR data based on that specific length-overrun check, so inputs that previously would have been marked invalid may now pass this validation step.

Remove the TLV field length overrun validation from `tlv_data_is_valid()`.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it hardens TLV parsing by rejecting records whose declared length exceeds the remaining buffer, preventing out-of-bounds access during MGMT advertising TLV validation.

The root cause is an out-of-bounds read in tlv_data_is_valid() due to insufficient length validation before accessing the next byte. This change removes that overrun check, directly relating to the vulnerable parsing logic.

This is the same unsafe pattern in the TLV parser: it reads the type byte at i+1 without first validating that the length-delimited field covers that index.

The vulnerable root cause was an out-of-bounds read from `data[i + 1]` before verifying that the current TLV element actually contained that byte. In this snippet, the loop still does `cur_len = data[i];` and immediately accesses `data[i + 1]` in `if (data[i + 1] == EIR_FLAGS && ... )`, so the bounds-checking issue is not addressed here. However, the code shown is about advertising-instance validity for flags, not the missing length check itself; the new condition `(!is_adv_data || flags_managed(adv_flags))` only changes when flags are rejected and does not add a guard against `i + 1` being out of range. Since the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not fixed by this diff and the snippet does not show the length-validation logic that would prevent it, this function does not contain the fix.
